paper_metadata.title: LiT: Zero-Shot Transfer with Locked-image text Tuning
paper_metadata.abstract: This paper presents contrastive-tuning, a simple method employing contrastive training to align image and text models while still taking advantage of their pre-training. In our empirical study we find that locked pre-trained image models with unlocked text models work best. We call this instance of contrastive-tuning "Locked-image Tuning" (LiT), which just teaches a text model to read out good representations from a pre-trained image model for new tasks. A LiT model gains the capability of zero-shot transfer to new vision tasks, such as image classification or retrieval. The proposed LiT is widely applicable; it works reliably with multiple pre-training methods (supervised and unsupervised) and across diverse architectures (ResNet, Vision Transformers and MLP-Mixer) using three different image-text datasets. With the transformer-based pre-trained ViT-g/14 model, the LiT model achieves 85.2% zero-shot transfer accuracy on the ImageNet test set, and 82.5% on the challenging out-of-distribution ObjectNet test set.

extraction_data.innovation: Locked-image Tuning (LiT): A contrastive-tuning method that freezes a pre-trained image model (image tower) and trains only a text model (text tower) to align with image representations, making it highly data- and compute-efficient compared to training both towers from scratch or fine-tuning the image model.

extraction_data.innovation: Locked-image text tuning (LiT): freezes a pre-trained image encoder and only fine-tunes the text encoder during contrastive learning, drastically reducing trainable parameters and training time while maintaining or improving zero-shot transfer performance compared to fully fine-tuned or from-scratch models.
